title: Ledger event v1.1
description: One line of var/loopqueue/ledger.jsonl. Append-only, NEVER rewritten - it is the history, and it wins over state/queue.json. Append only through bridge/ledger_write.py, which serializes writers with locks/ledger.lock, checks short writes, and fsyncs before success; readers must tolerate a torn final line after a crash. Put bulk output in receipts/ and reference the path.

event.$comment: `answered` closes an inquiry once a proposal carrying answers_inquiry is written; every inquiry must reach `answered` or `rejected` or inquiries/ grows forever. `unparked` records a human releasing a parked item - the attempt counter is derived from rejections SINCE the latest unparked, so without this event the producer recounts old rejections and re-parks immediately. `completed` is a TERMINAL event (alongside `merged`/`rejected`) for out-of-repo / host-ops work that was VERIFIED and APPLIED but legitimately has no merge_sha - unlike `merged` it carries NO detail.merge_sha, and unlike `rejected` it is not a refusal (no TTL/class). It follows the same 7-day terminal retention as `merged`. `closed` is the FINDING-side terminal event: emitted on a FINDING id by the gate loop when a candidate that resolves it lands AND the finding's bound test ran GREEN in that gate run. It carries detail.closed_by (the candidate id), detail.merge_sha, and detail.bound_test. It is never emitted by an agent by hand and never on a proposal/candidate id - those terminalise with merged/rejected/completed. `isolated` is a NON-TERMINAL routing marker emitted per member of a multi-member candidate-defect train that was ISOLATED instead of mass-rejected: it records that the member must re-gate SOLO and carries detail.isolation_members (the complete sorted group, so any one surviving event reconstructs it). It grants NO landing permission, produces NO queue status, and is NOT terminal - the member keeps its prior status until it reaches merged/rejected/completed. Read only by the gate loop's _pending_isolation_ids. It requires no detail-bearing allOf block (base fields ts/role/event/id suffice).

id.description: Required for every event EXCEPT instrument_error, which often has no artifact (provider down, disk full).

actor.description: process, model, or person that emitted the event

expires_at.description: MANDATORY on rejected. A rejection without a TTL is a permanent ban. After expiry the idea may be RE-ARGUED with new evidence and an explicit supersedes - never resubmitted unchanged.

exit_code.description: 2 means DO NOT RETRY THIS INPUT

alerted.description: parked - true once, ever. Repeated alerts train the operator to ignore them.

remedy.description: What the producer should DO. 'replan' = fix the named gap and resubmit with supersedes. 'drop' = eliminate the idea; the TTL is the earliest it may be RE-ARGUED with new evidence, not a retry timer. 'blocked' = wait on a named dependency. Producers assume 'replan' when absent, and then burn attempts polishing an idea you meant to kill.

isolation_members.description: Present on an `isolated` event: the COMPLETE sorted member group of the isolated train, so any one surviving event reconstructs the whole set. Defense-in-depth for the reader's own validation - a non-empty array of canonical sha256 ids. The gate loop's _ledger_isolated_active SKIPS a single malformed event (building membership from the well-formed ones) and only VETOES when no usable isolation source remains at all - it does NOT raise on one bad line, which would permanently halt dispatch on an append-only ledger; schema validation is the second lens, not the only one.

allOf.$comment: every event except instrument_error names an artifact
